description: Versioned provenance for code extracted out of src/recommendation/ into packages/. One batch per extraction PR, and each batch keeps its own immutable baseline commit, its source -> destination pairs and the identity policy those pairs must satisfy. A later PR APPENDS a batch; a merged batch is never rewritten, so PR 2's baseline cannot drift when PR 3 or PR 4 is measured.

batches.description: Step 4B PR 2: the pure candidates modules, the Engine 1 compatibility tree and the pure half of filtering moved into packages/recommendation-core/src/, leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. Nothing here is a rewrite: each destination is the same bytes as the source at the baseline.

characterization.capture_commit_subject: test(core): freeze the PR 2 surface before anything moves

batches.description: Step 4B PR 3: the pure Engine 3 assembly stage moved into packages/recommendation-core/src/assembly/, leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. Its only intra-tree dependencies (../candidates/*, ../filtering/*) already live in the core package, so every relative specifier resolves unchanged from the destination: nothing here is a rewrite.

characterization.capture_commit_subject: test(core): freeze the assembly surface before anything moves

batches.description: Step 4B PR 4: the Engine 5a ranking stage moved into packages/recommendation-core/src/ranking/ - the barrel plus its three stage modules (ranking, diverse top-set selection and archetype selection) - leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. Its only intra-tree dependencies (../assembly, ../candidates/errors) already live in the core package, so every relative specifier resolves unchanged from the destination: nothing here is a rewrite.

characterization.capture_commit_subject: test(core): freeze the ranking surface before anything moves

batches.description: Step 4B PR 5: the Engine 2D retention stage moved into packages/recommendation-core/src/retention/ - the barrel plus its four stage modules (per-role retention, the budget floor diagnostic, the E2 per-role price targets and the E6 iGPU eligibility set) - leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. Its whole dependency graph (../candidates/{select,roles,errors}, ../filtering/filter, ../assembly/prices) already lives in the core package, so all 15 relative specifiers resolve unchanged from the destination: nothing here is a rewrite. Four contract suites moved with the modules; retain.test.js stays in the runtime suite because it imports ../scoring/candidate-score, which has not been extracted yet.

characterization.capture_commit_subject: test(core): freeze the retention surface before anything moves

batches.description: Step 4B PR 6: the pure half of Engine 4 scoring moved into packages/recommendation-core/src/scoring/ - the Decision 3(a) configuration validator, the Decision 37 use-case vocabulary, and the STEP 1-3 effective/candidate/build score modules - leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. Their whole dependency graph (../candidates/{errors,roles}, ../assembly/assemble, ./effective-score) already lives in the core package, so all 13 relative specifiers resolve unchanged from the destination: nothing here is a rewrite. The mixed runtime barrel (scoring/index.js) and its two SQL loaders stay in the runtime tree untouched, and a hand-written 14-key core barrel publishes only the pure surface. Five scoring contract suites moved with the modules, and the deferred retain.test.js moved too: its single scoring import (../scoring/candidate-score) is now a core module.

characterization.capture_commit_subject: test(core): freeze the scoring surface before anything moves

batches.description: Step 4B PR 7: the four pure Engine 6 explanation modules (build-facts, explain, reasons, index) and offers/as-of.js moved into packages/recommendation-core/src/explanation/ and packages/recommendation-core/src/offers/, leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. Two barrel imports were narrowed BEFORE this baseline (../assembly -> ../assembly/assemble, ../ranking -> ../ranking/select-archetypes), so every relative specifier resolves unchanged from the destination: nothing here is a rewrite. offers/select.js and the runtime offers barrel stay in the runtime tree untouched; the core entry point publishes `explanation` and `offers` (the as-of module itself, with no core offers/index.js). Four explanation/as-of suites moved with the modules.

characterization.capture_commit_subject: test(core): freeze the explanation and as-of surface before anything moves

batches.description: Step 5 W1: the Engine 2 stage 1 offer pre-selection query (selectOfferPrices, the single parameterized store_offer query) moved out of src/recommendation/offers/ into packages/recommendation-runtime/src/offers/, leaving an identity re-export shim at the old path. It is database-backed, so it belongs to the runtime package, not the pure core. The move is byte-identical because the import specifiers were made location-independent BEFORE this baseline: commit 'refactor(offers): reach core through the core-entry adapter' added src/recommendation/core-entry.js and rewrote the module's five requires into one '../core-entry' require, so the same bytes resolve the core package root from either depth (the runtime tree answers the same specifier with its own packages/recommendation-runtime/src/core-entry.js). Behaviour is pinned by the L1 suite src/recommendation/offers/select.test.js - the Decision 65 selection tests among them - which needs an injected fake client, and by the DB-free packages/recommendation-runtime/test/offers-select.test.js added in this batch. No characterization fixture is recorded: a module whose whole contract is exercised through an injected client needs no captured surface beyond the suites that already run in CI.

Step 5 W1 PR 1: the two query loaders (the pinned recommendation_query lookup and the Decision 47 catalog content digest) and the two scoring loaders (the pinned scoring_model lookup and the candidate-scoped component_assessment read) moved out of src/recommendation/{query,scoring}/ into packages/recommendation-runtime/src/{query,scoring}/, leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. All four execute SQL, so they belong to the runtime package, not the pure core. The move is byte-identical because the import specifiers were made location-independent BEFORE this baseline: commit 'refactor(query,scoring): reach core through the core-entry adapter' rewrote each module's core requires into one '../core-entry' require, so the same bytes resolve the core package root from either depth (the runtime tree answers the same specifier with its own packages/recommendation-runtime/src/core-entry.js). Behaviour is pinned by the four L1 suites that stayed at the old paths - they inject a fake client and now exercise the modules through the shims - and by the four DB-free suites added under packages/recommendation-runtime/test/ in this batch. No characterization fixture is recorded: a module whose whole contract is exercised through an injected client needs no captured surface beyond the suites that already run in CI.

Step 5 W1 PR 2: the two remaining loaders that feed Engine 2 - the Engine 2B candidate loader (loadCandidates, which derives a candidate's category from canonical spec-table presence and issues one statement per required role plus the canonical-category ambiguity guard) and the Engine 2D filtering-context loader (loadFilteringContext with its CONTEXT_COMPAT_KEYS vocabulary, which loads candidate-scoped specs, the socket->platform map and the seven compatibility buckets) - moved out of src/recommendation/{candidates,filtering}/ into packages/recommendation-runtime/src/{candidates,filtering}/, leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. Both execute SQL, so they belong to the runtime package, not the pure core. The move is byte-identical because the import specifiers were made location-independent BEFORE this baseline: commit 'refactor(candidates,filtering): reach core through the core-entry adapter' rewrote each module's four relative core requires into one '../core-entry' require, so the same bytes resolve the core package root from either depth (the runtime tree answers the same specifier with its own packages/recommendation-runtime/src/core-entry.js). Behaviour is pinned by the L1 suites that stayed at the old paths - src/recommendation/candidates/loader.test.js and src/recommendation/filtering/context-loader.test.js, which inject a fake client and now exercise the modules through the shims - and by the two DB-free suites added under packages/recommendation-runtime/test/ in this batch, which additionally freeze every statement's SQL text, its parameter array and the statement SEQUENCE (no test pinned that order before). No characterization fixture is recorded: a module whose whole contract is exercised through an injected client needs no captured surface beyond the suites that already run in CI.

Step 5 W1 PR 3: the three remaining modules of the W1 loaders namespace - the Engine 2D filtering composition (filterCandidatesForRecommendation, which composes the already-extracted filtering-context loader with the pure core filter) and the two runtime-only public barrels of the loaders (offers/index.js publishing selectOfferPrices and SELECT_OFFER_PRICES_SQL, query/index.js publishing the two query loaders with their SQL constants, REQUIRED_ROLES and the Decision 47 catalog vocabulary) - moved out of src/recommendation/{filtering,offers,query}/ into packages/recommendation-runtime/src/{filtering,offers,query}/, leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. The pipeline executes no SQL itself but is infrastructure composition owned at runtime/ (RFC 11.2), not a core member; both barrels publish SQL-executing members, so neither is a mixed barrel. The move is byte-identical relative to THIS batch's baseline, which is commit A on the branch: 'refactor(filtering): reach the core filter through the core-entry adapter' rewrote the pipeline's one core require into '../core-entry' so the same bytes resolve the core package root from either depth (the runtime tree answers the same specifier with its own packages/recommendation-runtime/src/core-entry.js). The two barrels needed no specifier change: their siblings (./select, ./load-query-input, ./catalog-version) had already moved into the same runtime directories in the earlier W1 batches, so each require resolves unchanged from the new depth. Behaviour is pinned by the L1 suites that stayed at the old paths - src/recommendation/filtering/pipeline.test.js, src/recommendation/offers/select.test.js and src/recommendation/query/*.test.js, which now exercise the modules through the shims - and by the three DB-free suites added under packages/recommendation-runtime/test/ in this batch: a recording fake client that pins the composition's single loader call, the identity of the client passed through, the statement sequence and that the pure filter issues no query; plus an export-key and function-identity comparison of each barrel against its old path. No characterization fixture is recorded: a module whose whole contract is exercised through an injected client needs no captured surface beyond the suites that already run in CI.

Step 5 W2: the five persistence modules - the three Engine 5b writers (persist-ranked's three batched UNNEST INSERTs, persist-pass-facts' UPDATE-only pass facts, persist-rejections' Decision 31 replace DELETE plus INSERT) and the two write-shaped payload validators (validate-selected, validate-rejections) - moved out of src/recommendation/persistence/ into packages/recommendation-runtime/src/persistence/, leaving identity re-export shims at the old paths. All five are runtime-owned: three execute DML on the caller's client and two are pure code whose contract is a write payload, which RFC 11.3 keeps out of the pure domain. They own no transaction boundary and touch no pool (proved before the move: no BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, no new Pool, no process.env read, one injected client), so orchestrator/commit.js keeps the single write transaction and this batch moves no behaviour. The move is byte-identical relative to THIS batch's baseline, which is commit A on the branch: 'refactor(persistence): reach the core through the core-entry adapter' rewrote the four core-importing modules' requires into one '../core-entry' require, so the same bytes resolve the core package root from either depth (the runtime tree answers the same specifier with its own packages/recommendation-runtime/src/core-entry). persist-ranked needed no specifier change. No persistence namespace is published: src/index.js still exports only `loaders`, because the RFC 11.5 persistence table is the W2 surface the orchestrator batch will need to slice, and publishing it here would fix a shape before its consumers exist. Behaviour is pinned by the L1 suites that stayed at the old paths - src/recommendation/persistence/*.test.js, which inject a recording fake client and now exercise the modules through the shims - and by the five DB-free suites added under packages/recommendation-runtime/test/ in this batch, which freeze each writer's exact SQL text, its parameter arrays and its statement ORDER, prove the old path is the same module by identity, and prove every validator accept/reject case yields the same result and the same error through both paths. No characterization fixture is recorded: a module whose whole contract is exercised through an injected client needs no captured surface beyond the suites that already run in CI.
